steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper TITAN-Next, which translates LiDAR point clouds into RGB-D camera images using scene semantics. Explain why LiDAR-to-camera translation is hard, list our contributions over TITAN-Net, and mention possible applications in autonomous driving.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Domain translation and the challenge of multi-modal (LiDAR to camera) translation
- Our approach: semantics as mid-level representation; TITAN-Next
- Contributions over TITAN-Net
- Novelty and practical applications

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Domain translation
  - converting images from one domain to a type-similar domain; sketches or segmentation masks -> RGB images (cite)
  - cross-domain image-to-image translation: much recent attention in computer vision and robotics
  - multi-modal setup (LiDAR <-> camera) still a challenge, in its infancy (cite)
  - LiDAR scans cannot capture rich texture of RGB images; 3D point clouds sparse, non-uniformly dispersed vs structured 2D images
  - -> image synthesis from raw point clouds non-trivial
- Our approach
  - scene semantics as mid-level representation between sensor modalities with unique data formats
  - TITAN-Next (generaTive domaIn TrANslation Network): depth- and semantics-aware conditional generative model
  - adversarially learns LiDAR point clouds -> RGB-D camera images, relying solely on semantic scene segments
  - built on TITAN-Net (cite), modular generative neural network framework; revised framework (Fig. 2) to predict depth concurrently + higher fidelity RGB
- Contributions
  - multi-scale feature pyramid module in TITAN-Net encoder and decoder; downsampled LiDAR input injected into each encoder level; decoder block features upsampled, concatenated with final output -> robustness, accuracy, convergence speed
  - lightweight depth head on decoder; depth derived directly from LiDAR input -> RGB-D images from point clouds
  - quantitative and qualitative evaluation on Semantic-KITTI (cite); outperforms TITAN-Net and strong baselines by a large margin; code and models at https://github.com/TiagoCortinhal/TITAN-Next
- Novelty and applications
  - first multi-modal domain translation framework generating photo-realistic RGB-D images from raw 3D point clouds relying solely on sensor agnostic semantics
  - autonomous vehicles: RGB and depth sensor failure -> substitute synthesized RGB-D streams for sensor fusion and planning; natural fail-safe, prevent system collapse
  - data augmentation in target image domain: semantic segments -> many variants of original scene from different distributions, no extra effort
  - colourize point clouds without real RGB camera readings

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
There have been several attempts to convert images from one domain to another domain of a similar type, which is called domain translation, for example mapping sketches or segmentation masks to RGB images. These cross-domain image-to-image translations have got a lot of attention recently in computer vision and in robotics. But cross-domain mapping in a multi-modal setup, for example between LiDAR and camera sensors, is still a challenge and is still in its infancy. The main challenge with LiDAR scans is that they cannot capture the rich texture details that RGB images have, so the 3D point clouds are sparse and non-uniformly dispersed, unlike the 2D images from RGB sensors which are more structured. Because of this, synthesizing images from raw point clouds is non-trivial. In this work we deal with the challenge of multi-modal domain translation by using the scene semantics as a mid-level representation between the different sensor modalities, which have unique data formats. We introduce a new conditional generative model that is depth- and semantics-aware, called TITAN-Next (generaTive domaIn TrANslation Network). It learns adversarially to translate LiDAR point clouds to RGB-D camera images by relying only on the semantic scene segments.

TITAN-Next is based on the model TITAN-Net, which is part of a modular generative neural network framework. Here we revise this modular framework (see Fig. 2) so that the original TITAN-Net also predicts the depth information at the same time as it generates RGB camera images with higher fidelity. Our contributions are the following:

- Contributions
  - multi-scale feature pyramid module in TITAN-Net encoder and decoder; downsampled LiDAR input injected into each encoder level; decoder block features upsampled, concatenated with final output -> robustness, accuracy, convergence speed
  - lightweight depth head on decoder; depth derived directly from LiDAR input -> RGB-D images from point clouds
  - quantitative and qualitative evaluation on Semantic-KITTI (cite); outperforms TITAN-Net and strong baselines by a large margin; code and models at https://github.com/TiagoCortinhal/TITAN-Next
- Novelty and applications
  - first multi-modal domain translation framework generating photo-realistic RGB-D images from raw 3D point clouds relying solely on sensor agnostic semantics
  - autonomous vehicles: RGB and depth sensor failure -> substitute synthesized RGB-D streams for sensor fusion and planning; natural fail-safe, prevent system collapse
  - data augmentation in target image domain: semantic segments -> many variants of original scene from different distributions, no extra effort
  - colourize point clouds without real RGB camera readings

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
There have been several attempts to convert images from one domain to another domain of a similar type, which is called domain translation, for example mapping sketches or segmentation masks to RGB images. These cross-domain image-to-image translations have got a lot of attention recently in computer vision and in robotics. But cross-domain mapping in a multi-modal setup, for example between LiDAR and camera sensors, is still a challenge and is still in its infancy. The main challenge with LiDAR scans is that they cannot capture the rich texture details that RGB images have, so the 3D point clouds are sparse and non-uniformly dispersed, unlike the 2D images from RGB sensors which are more structured. Because of this, synthesizing images from raw point clouds is non-trivial. In this work we deal with the challenge of multi-modal domain translation by using the scene semantics as a mid-level representation between the different sensor modalities, which have unique data formats. We introduce a new conditional generative model that is depth- and semantics-aware, called TITAN-Next (generaTive domaIn TrANslation Network). It learns adversarially to translate LiDAR point clouds to RGB-D camera images by relying only on the semantic scene segments.

TITAN-Next is based on the model TITAN-Net, which is part of a modular generative neural network framework. Here we revise this modular framework (see Fig. 2) so that the original TITAN-Net also predicts the depth information at the same time as it generates RGB camera images with higher fidelity. Our contributions are the following:

- We introduce a multi-scale feature pyramid module in the encoder and decoder of the original TITAN-Net. To make learning more stable and better at different scales, we inject a downsampled version of the LiDAR input into each encoder level. In the same way, we extract the features from each decoder block, upsample them and concatenate them with the final output. This multi-scale feature aggregation gives a significant improvement in robustness, accuracy and convergence speed.

- We also add a lightweight depth head to the TITAN-Net decoder, so that the generated scene image gets depth information which is derived directly from the LiDAR input. In the end this lets us generate RGB-D images from given point clouds.

- We report comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations on the large-scale and challenging Semantic-KITTI dataset. Our experiments show that the new framework outperforms the original TITAN-Net and other strong baselines by a large margin. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/TiagoCortinhal/TITAN-Next to encourage more research on the subject.

As far as we know, the multi-modal domain translation framework we propose is the first one that can generate photo-realistic RGB-D images from raw 3D point clouds by relying only on the sensor agnostic scene semantics. This has practical applications for autonomous vehicles. For example, if the RGB and depth sensors fail abruptly, the synthesized RGB-D image streams can be used immediately in their place to support the sensor fusion and planning modules that come after. This gives the vehicle a natural fail-safe mechanism to prevent a system collapse. Another possible application is augmenting the data that is available in the target image domain. The generated semantic scene segments can be used to create many variants of the original scene by feeding data from different distributions without any extra effort. The framework can also be used to colourize point clouds without relying on real RGB camera readings.

steps.text:
There have been several attempts to convert images from one domain to another domain of a similar type, which is called domain translation, for example mapping sketches or segmentation masks to RGB images [1,2,3]. These cross-domain image-to-image translations have got a lot of attention recently in computer vision and in robotics. But cross-domain mapping in a multi-modal setup, for example between LiDAR and camera sensors, is still a challenge and is still in its infancy [4,5,6,7]. The main challenge with LiDAR scans is that they cannot capture the rich texture details that RGB images have, so the 3D point clouds are sparse and non-uniformly dispersed, unlike the 2D images from RGB sensors which are more structured. Because of this, synthesizing images from raw point clouds is non-trivial. In this work we deal with the challenge of multi-modal domain translation by using the scene semantics as a mid-level representation between the different sensor modalities, which have unique data formats. It learns adversarially to translate LiDAR point clouds to RGB-D camera images by relying only on the semantic scene segments.

TITAN-Next is based on the model TITAN-Net [8], which is part of a modular generative neural network framework. Here we revise this modular framework (see Fig. 2) so that the original TITAN-Net also predicts the depth information at the same time as it generates RGB camera images with higher fidelity. Our contributions are the following:

- We introduce a multi-scale feature pyramid module in the encoder and decoder of the original TITAN-Net. To make learning more stable and better at different scales, we inject a downsampled version of the LiDAR input into each encoder level. - We also add a lightweight depth head to the TITAN-Net decoder, so that the generated scene image gets depth information which is derived directly from the LiDAR input. In the end this lets us generate RGB-D images from given point clouds.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
There are several attempts at converting images from one domain to another type-similar domain, known as domain translation, including mapping sketches or segmentation masks to RGB images [1,2,3]. Such cross-domain image-to-image translations have recently received significant attention in computer vision and robotics. However, cross-domain mapping in a multi-modal setup, for instance between LiDAR and camera sensors, is a challenge and still remains in its infancy [4,5,6,7]. The challenge with LiDAR scans stems primarily from their inability to capture the rich texture details that RGB images provide, resulting in 3D point clouds that are sparse and non-uniformly dispersed, unlike the more structured 2D images from RGB sensors. This makes image synthesis from raw point clouds non-trivial. In this work, we address the challenge of multi-modal domain translation by leveraging the scene semantics as a mid-level representation between different sensor modalities with unique data formats. To this end, we introduce a new depth- and semantics-aware conditional generative model, named TITAN-Next (generaTive domaIn TrANslation Network), which adversarially learns to translate LiDAR point clouds to RGB-D camera images by solely relying on the semantic scene segments (see Fig. -1).

TITAN-Next is built upon the model TITAN-Net [8], which is embedded in a modular generative neural network framework. Here we revise this modular framework (see Fig. 2) so that the original TITAN-Net concurrently predicts the depth information while generating RGB camera images with higher fidelity. More specifically, our contributions are:

- • We introduce a multi-scale feature pyramid module in the original TITAN-Net encoder and decoder. To enforce stability and improve learning at different scales, we inject a downsampled version of the LiDAR input into each level of the encoder. Similarly, we extract the features from each decoder block, upsample them, and concatenate them with the final output. This multi-scale feature aggregation yields a significant improvement in robustness, accuracy, and convergence speed.

- • We further append a lightweight depth head to the TITAN-Net decoder to enrich the generated scene image with depth information derived directly from the LiDAR input. This eventually leads to generating RGB-D images from given point clouds.

- • We report comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations on the large-scale, challenging Semantic-KITTI dataset [9]. Our experimental findings show that the new framework considerably outperforms the original TITAN-Net and other strong baselines by a large margin. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/TiagoCortinhal/TITAN-Next to encourage further research on the subject.

To the best of our knowledge, the proposed multi-modal domain translation framework is the first of its kind that can generate photo-realistic RGB-D images from raw 3D point clouds by solely relying on sensor agnostic scene semantics. This has practical applications in autonomous vehicles. For instance, in case of an abrupt failure of the RGB and depth sensors, the synthesized RGB-D image streams can immediately substitute them to boost the subsequent sensor fusion and planning modules, which gives the vehicle a natural fail-safe mechanism to prevent a system collapse. Another potential application is augmenting the available data in the target image domain: the generated semantic scene segments can be employed to fabricate vast variants of the original scene by feeding data from different distributions without any additional effort. Furthermore, the framework can be applied to colourize point clouds without relying on real RGB camera readings.
